title: Edge-cusped compactons from gradient-power nonlinear dispersion: exact transitions and singular spectral structure
abstract: We introduce a conservative two-exponent dispersive family, with $p>1$ the nonlinear-flux exponent and $r>0$ the gradient-dispersion exponent, that separates the mechanisms governing compactification, free-boundary regularity and linearised spectral structure while retaining an explicit travelling-wave theory. The family reduces to the absolute Rosenau-Hyman equation when $r=1$. The deformation leaves the amplitude-speed law unchanged, but makes the width amplitude dependent except at $r=1$. Two independent transition curves emerge: $pr=1$ separates infinite-tail solitary waves from compactons, whereas $r(p-1)=2$ separates compactons with a regular free boundary from edge-cusped compactons with divergent slope. The latter remain distributional solutions, with no singular measures at either the free boundary or the crest. For $r\ge1$, the linearisation factors through a singular Sturm-Liouville operator whose natural Friedrichs realisation is solvable: after a compacton-adapted change of variable, the eigenvalue equation is of Jacobi-hypergeometric type, with two explicit spectral sequences, exactly one negative eigenvalue and a one-dimensional translation kernel. Numerical experiments connect these exact structures to approximation and dynamics. Measured Fourier tails and projection errors agree with the rates predicted by the free-boundary exponent, while padded Fourier-Galerkin time integration propagates the cusped waves coherently with small phase drift. A structure-adapted Jacobi-Galerkin diagnostic of the full generator finds no detectable real part in the tested truncated point spectra. The family therefore provides an explicit testbed in which geometric singularity, weak admissibility, spectral structure and numerical regularity of compactons can be studied within a single degenerate dispersive model.
summary: This paper develops a generalized nonlinear dispersive model to study 'compactons'—solitary wave solutions with compact support. It achieves this by independently controlling parameters that govern the wave's support, its boundary regularity, and its associated spectral properties. The work is significant for providing a unified mathematical testbed to analyze complex phenomena like geometric singularities and spectral structure in nonlinear wave dynamics.
main_problem: The study aims to independently analyze and separate the mechanisms governing compactification, free-boundary regularity, and linearized spectral structure within a single, degenerate nonlinear dispersive model.
main_result: The authors introduce a two-exponent family of equations that allows for the controlled study of geometric singularities, weak admissibility, and spectral properties in compacton solutions.
method: The analysis combines analytical techniques (solving ODEs for travelling waves) with advanced numerical methods, including Fourier-Galerkin time integration and Jacobi-Galerkin spectral diagnostics.
model_or_system: The system is governed by a nonlinear dispersive equation involving two exponents, $p$ (nonlinear-flux) and $r$ (gradient-dispersion), which yields 'edge-cusped compactons' solutions.
key_observables: Mass $M[u]$, conserved quantity $Q[u]$, spectral eigenvalues, and the decay rates of the high-frequency Fourier tail.
important_parameters: The critical parameters are the exponents $p>1$ and $r>0$, and the transition curves $pr=1$ and $r(p-1)=2$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a travelling-wave solution and treats the problem as a testbed for separating different types of mathematical singularities.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the coherent propagation of cusped waves over time, the algebraic decay of Fourier coefficients controlled by the free boundary, and the convergence of computed eigenvalues towards exact spectral values.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the general model and its conserved quantities, then derives the explicit form of the travelling-wave solution (compacton), followed by a detailed spectral analysis of the linearized operator, and finally, numerical verification of the solution's stability and regularity.
why_interesting: While not directly about quantum systems, the rigorous mathematical framework developed for studying singular solutions, spectral theory (Jacobi-hypergeometric type), and weak admissibility in nonlinear PDEs provides powerful tools applicable to analyzing quantum field theories or non-equilibrium quantum dynamics where singular limits are encountered.
